title: Crosswalk constraints 1:1 notes - pre-roundtable
body:
Purpose: quick notes for 1:1s before cross-functional roundtable (Product + Eng + Applied ML). Goal is to surface constraints that will affect Q3 sequencing and identify blockers we can remove this week.

Meeting context:
- Roundtable scheduled: 2026-04-22 09:30 PT (all-hands for roadmap sequencing)
- This doc = my scratch for 1:1s on 4/20-4/21; capture rough asks and crisp asks to bring to the table.

Attendees to prep with (I will talk to each):
- Marco Chen (Eng: serving-runtime) — high priority
- Priya Desai (Applied ML: model onboarding) — high priority
- Samir Kaur (Product: Dedicated & Private offerings) — medium
- Optional: Quinn (SRE) if we hit infra quotas discussion

Key threads to surface in roundtable (short bullets I want people to commit to):
1) Model onboarding pipeline timeline (Priya)
   - Ask: Can applied-ml commit to publishing a verified quantized artifact for the new 13B variant by 2026-05-10?
   - Risk: Without verified artifact, Dedicated pools can't schedule stable deployments for the center of mass (QPS-heavy customers).
   - Constraint: CI GPU time limited to 1k hours / month; need to prioritize which models get verification runs.

2) Inference latency budget vs batching (Marco)
   - Ask: Can runtime support a per-customer latency SLO override (e.g., 95th p95 target of 120ms) that opts out of some batching heuristics?
   - Tradeoff: Lower batching reduces cost efficiency. Need clear cost delta per override so product can price/offer.

3) Canary rollout policy gaps (Samir)
   - Ask: Product wants canary window (traffic inc) to be reduced from 72h to 24h for emergency patches. Engineering needs checks we can run automatically.
   - Constraint: Monitoring retention and trace sampling currently too low to give confidence in 24h windows for small-volume customers.

4) KV prefix caching and cross-tenant memory pressure (Marco + Priya)
   - Observation: Applied-ML evals show ~12% token cost savings with prefix cache for certain prompt families, but memory pressure on nodes spikes with multiple tenants using long prefixes.
   - Ask: agree on a max-prefix-length or token-budget per tenant; engineering & runtime to propose throttling behavior by 4/27.

5) Benchmarks & regression gate (Priya + Product)
   - Ask: Define minimal eval suite (3 prompt families, 2 automatic metrics, 1 human-smoke test) that must pass before model rollout to Dedicated.
   - Decision needed: who owns the human-smoke test? Applied-ML wants product to supply 10 sentinel prompts from real customers.

Open questions I'm bringing to 1:1s (what I need answers to):
- Which customers are blockers for the 13B rollout (list/name)? Product/Sales to provide narrow list — otherwise we prioritize incorrectly.
- Is there temporary capacity (burst pool) for two weeks to run onboarding/verification without impacting production SLAs? (Infra request)
- If we reduce canary to 24h, what auto-checks are non-negotiable? (logs, error rate thresholds, latency regressions >= 10%)

Notes from quick calls so far (raw):
- Marco: "We can add per-customer SLO override but requires separate request queue + feature flag. ETA ~3 sprints if prioritized."
- Priya: "We can compress verification if we accept lower sampling of generation seeds; risk missing rare regressions."
- Samir: "Product can tighten canary desires if engineering gives exact list of checks; we can trade a longer manual review window for fewer auto-checks."

Decision proposals I plan to push in roundtable (short, concrete):
A) Prioritize verification for top-5 high-QPS customers for 13B (Priya + Sales to supply list by 2026-04-22 EOD).
B) Pilot per-customer latency override on 1 Dedicated pool (Marco) with explicit cost uplift displayed in Console for customers; pilot start 2026-05-04.
C) Agree to implement an automatic canary-check bundle (error-rate spike, p95 latency delta, token consumption anomaly) as the minimum for 24h canary; exact thresholds to be decided by engineering by 2026-04-28.
D) Enforce a 16k token-prefix budget per tenant for prefix-caching in the short term; runtime to emit metric spikes to #prod-eng-rollouts for telemetry.

Follow-ups / Action items (owner -> task -> due):
- Priya Desai -> Publish prioritized model verification queue + highlight which models will be deferred (include rationale) -> due 2026-04-23.
- Marco Chen -> Scoping doc for per-customer SLO override (design + cost calc + feature-flag plan) -> draft 2026-04-27.
- Samir Kaur -> Customer list for top-5 QPS customers impacted by 13B -> 2026-04-22 EOD.
- Elena Park (me) -> Compile short briefing deck (3 slides) for 4/22 roundtable covering A-D proposals -> 2026-04-21 morning.
- Quinn (SRE) -> Confirm whether temporary burst pool can be allocated for verification CI (resource + ops runbook) -> 2026-04-24.
- Product Analytics -> Provide baseline usage matrix (per-customer QPS, avg sequence length, percentile token cost) -> 2026-04-23.

Risks / mitigation notes (to mention quickly):
- If verification is delayed, Dedicated customers may face unpredictable rollbacks or need emergency fallbacks to smaller models. Mitigation: automated fallback policy + clear customer communication template (Samir to draft).
- Cost vs latency tradeoffs risk revenue: show Product the delta in Console before enabling overrides so customers can opt-in knowingly.

Quick prep checklist for each 1:1 (what I will ask in the first 2 minutes):
- "What is the single blocker you can't resolve in 48 hours?"
- "If we had to choose one compromise (cost, timeline, scope), which would you pick?"
- "Who else needs to be looped in immediately if we proceed?"

Scratch brainstorming (ideas to float, not commitments):
- Short-term harmony: offer a paid "low-latency" tier that uses isolated pools (clear cost uplift) so we can preserve batching efficiency for the rest.
- Longer-term: build a cost-visibility endpoint in API so customers can see per-request expected token cost given their chosen SLO.

Decision record (tentative):
- If roundtable agrees to A-D proposals, create a tracked EPIC in JIRA linking INF-9876 and assign owners above.

Notes-to-self before roundtable:
- Keep language concrete and avoid "we should" statements — use "we will" with dates.
- Ask for hard commitments in the form of "I will deliver X by Y".
- Bring one slide showing the customer impact scenario (top-3 customers, cost/latency delta if override turned on).

End of scratch.

-- Elena
(leave this doc for quick edits after 1:1s; I'll copy into roundtable brief)
